title: Tax Exemption Certificates and Sales Tax Credits — Northgate Business Invoice Accounts (Net Terms) Tax Standard
content:
**Standard.** On Northgate Business Invoice Accounts (Net Terms), tax-exempt purchasing applies only while a certificate covering the order's ship-to or store state is on file and no more than the tier's certificate validity, in months, has passed since its issue date; after that the status becomes certificate expired and tax is charged until a new certificate is filed. Sales tax charged on an invoice is credited when a valid certificate covering the invoice date is filed no later than the tier's tax refund window, in days, after that invoice date, at most once per invoice. A Northgate+ Business membership's tax-exempt checkout relies on this same certificate. This applies where the tier supports tax-exempt purchasing, with certificates covering the states the tier names: the state of the store or the shipping destination of the order.

## Certificate status on the account

| Exemption status on record | Meaning |
|---|---|
| None | No certificate is recorded |
| Certificate on file | A certificate is recorded, with the date it was issued |
| Certificate expired | More than the validity period has passed since the issue date; tax is charged until a new certificate is filed |

A certificate is recorded, renewed or marked expired as its status changes.

## Exempt purchasing: conditions together

| Certificate on file covers the order's ship-to or store state | Time since issue date within the validity period | Tax-exempt purchasing |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Applies |
| Yes | No | Does not apply; tax is charged |
| No | Yes | Does not apply |

*Hypothetical (36-month validity):* an order placed 30 months after a certificate's issue date, shipping to the state the certificate covers, is purchased tax-exempt; an order placed 40 months after that issue date is charged tax until a new certificate is filed.

## Crediting tax already charged

The sales tax charged on an invoice is credited when a valid certificate covering the invoice date is filed no later than the refund window after that invoice date, and at most once per invoice. The credit reduces the amount the business owes on its invoice account.

*Hypothetical (90-day window):* an invoice dated 1 April that charged $48.00 of sales tax; a valid certificate covering 1 April is filed on 20 May, inside the window, and the $48.00 is credited once. A certificate filed the following November is outside the window for that invoice.
